Nine tasks coded in-session with ZERO subagents; ONE subagent, the close reviewer, at 181,605 tokens / 37 tool calls / 10.5 min. Main-session cost UNMEASURED (runbook O3): this row is NOT comparable to 09's 6.37M. THE ROI LINE: that single agent found THREE CRITICALs in code that had already passed eleven green `pnpm verify` runs and eight green CI runs — a stale medicineId speaking for a line, priors resolved by text alone, and a deactivated moiety emptying a composition in silence. The phase's 14 mutants all DIED, i.e. they confirmed assertions that were already right; the reviewer REFUTED. Confirmation and refutation are different purchases and the second is the one that was missing. Ledger at close: 329,574 bytes = 82k tokens re-billed per agent per call in any HEAVY successor (2.101).

Four tasks coded in-session with ZERO subagents; ONE reviewer, RESUMED once, across two passes: 206,146 tokens / 83 calls (~2,480 per call) then 268,625 / 30 calls (~8,950 per call) — the second is dearer per call because a RESUMED agent starts full (§2.108). Main-session cost UNMEASURED — not comparable to 09's 6.37M. STOP-LOSS 340,000, BREACHED BY 40%, entirely on the two review passes — and they are the reason the phase is correct: its four tasks produced five dead mutants, five green `pnpm verify` runs and four green CI runs over a tree carrying a MAJOR (T2's own re-key dropped counterparty separation from the accrual subject, so a second partner summed the first's rows as its own prior and was short-paid by exactly that amount). Pass 1 found that, plus 1 inherited MAJOR, 3 MINOR, 3 NOTE. Pass 2 — over the REMEDIATION, which was unreviewed code on the same money path — found a race test sitting 9s inside a 15s budget (green on an idle host, red on a busy runner; §2.99 about to repeat), a mutant that SURVIVED proving a comment claimed a discrimination it did not have, and an unenforced invariant now enforced by a composite FK. THE ROI LINE: the reviewer found more defects than the tasks did, and its single most valuable finding was in the fix for its own first finding. Ledger §2.107-§2.110; EXECUTE-METHOD-V3 §6 gains a review-budget term, §9.5 the resumed-agent rule.

Main-session cost UNMEASURED (runbook O3) — NOT comparable to 09's 6.37M. THE COST CURVE IS THE FINDING (2.115): workload fell ~2 orders of magnitude from pass 1 to pass 3 while total cost ROSE 28% and per-call cost rose 24x, because a resume re-bills a transcript that now contains the agent's own previous report. Two owner-authorised production deploys with the T7 precondition run read-only in between. Ledger 2.115-2.118; EXECUTE-METHOD-V3 9.5 gains the resume-for-memory/fresh-for-scope rule and a 1.3x-per-resume budget term.

Nine tasks coded in-session with ZERO coding subagents; TWO reviewers, both FRESH, NEITHER RESUMED — 244,568 tokens / 67 calls / 838s (close) and 213,923 / 72 / 1,058s (remediation). Main-session cost UNMEASURED (runbook O3) — NOT comparable to 09's 6.37M. STOP-LOSS 675,000, NOT BREACHED: 458,491, with 32% of headroom unused — the first phase since 16a to come in under, and the direct result of §2.115's fresh-not-resumed rule (13 spent 604,655 on ONE agent resumed twice, whose per-call cost rose 24x as its workload fell 2 orders of magnitude). THE ROI LINE: pass 1 returned 1 CRITICAL + 9 MAJOR + 8 MINOR against a tree that was NINE-for-nine green on pnpm verify AND on CI by full SHA, with every CRITICAL task's mutants built and killed and sixteen findings already self-reported. The CRITICAL is a silent stock loss: postMovements wrote an application-computed ABSOLUTE balance through an upsert and SELECT … FOR UPDATE cannot lock a row that does not exist, so two concurrent receipts into a NEW (store,batch) pair both read 0 and both wrote q — ledger 2q, balance q, and the loss lands HIGH so the non-negative CHECK never fires. Mutant DIED at {ledgerSum:10, balance:5}. Pass 2, over the REMEDIATION, returned a MAJOR the remediation's own commit message had claimed as fixed: M6 moved the GRN menu permission in the manifest and not in the SPA's hard-coded NAV table, so DD11's QC signatory still had no link — third consecutive phase (09a, 13, 14) whose worst late defect is inside the fix for an earlier finding. The executing session ALSO found two defects in the handed-off remediation before either reviewer saw it, by RUNNING it: the C1 fix failed 13 tests because a CHECK is evaluated against the proposed tuple before ON CONFLICT resolves, and the M2 fix made a recovery reachable that would have raised 25P02 on an aborted transaction. Ledger 2.119-2.124; EXECUTE-METHOD-V3 gains §9.6 (a handoff spends its last budget on RUNNING, not on writing). ARCHIVE pass retired §2.28 and explicitly KEPT §2.38.

Nine tasks coded in-session with ZERO coding subagents; TWO reviewers, both FRESH, NEITHER RESUMED - 271,994 tokens / 77 calls / 874s (close) and 191,515 / 53 / 660s (remediation). Main-session cost UNMEASURED (runbook O3) - NOT comparable to a HEAVY phase. STOP-LOSS 730,000, NOT BREACHED: 463,509, 36% of headroom unused, and within 1.1% of Plan 14's 458,491 for the same shape - the review cost is now flat phase-on-phase while the findings rose (14: 1 CRITICAL + 10 MAJOR across both passes; 15: 1 CRITICAL + 17 MAJOR + 26 MINOR). THE ROI LINE: pass 1 ran against a tree that was 8-for-8 green on pnpm verify AND CI by full SHA, with 22 mutants built and 21 killed, and returned a CRITICAL in the money path anyway - the Sec 269ST cash ceiling could not see cash taken at discharge, because the quantity it compared was summed only from deposits HELD. The Assertion Book had a row for that guard and its mutant DIED: the row asked whether the refusal fires, which is the question the plan's author had already thought about. Nobody had asked what the compared number was summed FROM (ledger 2.128; v3 9.7 makes it a standing instruction in the reviewer brief). Pass 2, over the REMEDIATION, returned SIX MAJORs and all six were inside pass 1's own fixes - fourth consecutive phase (09a, 13, 14, 15) with that shape. The worst two: an `additionalBill` flag added to excuse a double-submit emitted a FULL DUPLICATE CHARGE because composeDischargeBill knows nothing of what is already invoiced (flag removed, N13 carried to 15d), and a kernel guard stopping a blocked theatre from being reassigned left the one-theatre unit PERMANENTLY UNUSABLE with the refusal naming an action no route provided (returnTheatreToService ships with it). Also: pass 1's claim that the new per-receipt deposit bound dominates the patient-level one was FALSE (advanceOf subtracts refunds, a receipt balance does not) and had been written into a rewritten test - ledger 2.126. Three defects the executing session found before any reviewer, each proved fail-first: a kernel occupancy race affecting every bed/room/theatre, billing's missing advance-at-issue path (the whole deposit-then-discharge design was unreachable), and a count-mismatch incident rolled back by its own refusal. Tests 2,138 -> 2,398 core. Migrations 0035/0036/0037, all additive. CODE-COMPLETE, NOT DEPLOYED. Ledger 2.125-2.128; EXECUTE-METHOD-V3 gains 9.7 (brief the reviewer at the OPERANDS, not the branches) and 9.8 (a close-review fix is not done when it compiles - run the suite and read the count).
